issues.subject: The mind is not a camera
issues.preheader: What witnesses remember—and what surviving records can actually establish.
issues.excerpt: Memory can feel like a recording, but it is not a complete record. Puységur’s surviving files show why observation and explanation deserve separate questions. Read the historical source trail before deciding what the witnesses proved.

issues.subject: Before hypnosis had a name
issues.preheader: Eighteenth-century witnesses, sincere observations, and the problem of proof.
issues.excerpt: A witness can describe something sincerely and still mistake its cause. The Puységur files preserve that gap between what people reported and what they concluded. Read the archival account and judge the evidence yourself.

issues.subject: Fourteen seconds. A much longer explanation.
issues.preheader: Apollo 1 and the evidence that a single image cannot explain.
issues.excerpt: Apollo 1 left a record far richer than a single photograph. Examine the hatch, the fire, and the safety decisions without reducing the investigation to one easy cause. Read the historical evidence behind the tragedy.

issues.subject: What did seven days of attention reveal?
issues.preheader: Record what happened, including the days that did not go to plan.
issues.excerpt: An attention log is valuable when it records what happened, including days the routine did not work. Compare seven days without treating a pleasant session as proof of a product’s effect. Read the Fieldbook follow-up and make an evidence log of your own.
